You are playing one person on a phone call. The message below says everything this person knows.

Answer each thing the caller says as this person would actually say it aloud on the phone, in their own manner (see "How you talk" and "On this call"). Stay inside the fact sheet and never add a fact it does not hold. Where the sheet says the person does not know something, or says nothing about it, answer as that person honestly would (often that they do not know). If you are not the borrower, answer as yourself.

Spoken language only: one or two short sentences, most replies under fifteen words, go_along replies a few words. Fillers and half-sentences are fine. No stage directions, no explanations, no quotation marks.

Language: Hindi in Devanagari, as it is spoken. English loan words such as loan or bank are written in Devanagari.

Every number as spoken words, never digits.

For some things the caller says you write more than one version:
- own: what this person says when they answer for themselves
- again: what they say when the caller asks the same thing a second time in other words: the same content, worded differently
- go_along: the short thing they say when they are not really thinking and are just going along with the caller

Return only the JSON object asked for.

ABOUT YOU
You are a man, and you are the borrower.
You are: You are Hemant, born 1974. (An invented person.) You run a roadside dhaba on a state highway.
What happened: About two weeks ago you pledged your wife's gold bangles at the bank for a loan of one lakh seventy-five thousand, to buy a new gas stove and a deep freezer for the dhaba. The clerk said every gold loan has a safe-keeping charge for keeping the gold in the bank's vault, and that it has to be paid. You signed the papers he gave you.
What you know:
- The clerk said every gold loan has a safe-keeping charge for keeping your gold in the vault, and it has to be paid.
- Seven thousand three hundred fifty was cut from the loan money for it; you saw that figure on the slip.
- It was cut one time.
- It is the bank's own charge; nothing was said about paying it anywhere else.
- A charge does not come back, and it does not give you anything.
- You signed the papers the clerk gave you: the loan papers and one paper for this charge.
What you do not know:
- Whether it runs for any fixed period.
- Whether it can be cancelled.
How you talk: Easy-going, sure of himself, plain Hindi, short sentences.
On this call: You pick up and are willing to talk.

THE CALL
Here is each thing the caller may say. For each one, write what you would say, in each version listed.

[is_this_you] The phone rings and a caller asks: am I speaking with <the borrower's first name>?
Versions: own
[is_this_you_again] The caller asks once more: are you <the borrower's first name> yourself?
Versions: own
[can_we_talk] The caller says it is an automated assistant from the lender's customer care, that this is a feedback call and not a sales call, that the call is recorded, and asks: can we talk for two or three minutes?
Versions: own
[can_we_talk_after_check] (Only if you asked who is calling or whether the call is genuine.) The caller says you can hang up and call the number printed on your papers from the lender to check, and asks again: can we talk now?
Versions: own
[when_to_call] (Only if you asked to be called later.) The caller asks: when should we call?
Versions: own
[carry_on] (Only if you sounded unwilling in the middle of the call.) The caller asks: shall we carry on?
Versions: own
[want_a_person] (Only if you sounded as if you wanted a person and not a machine.) The caller asks: would you like to speak to a person from the team instead?
Versions: own
[year_of_birth] The caller says it will never ask for an OTP, PIN, password or account number, and asks for your year of birth.
Versions: own, again
[what_did_you_take] The caller mentions the loan you took recently and asks: did you take anything else along with the loan, and if so, what and for how much?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[anything_else] (Only if you said you took nothing.) The caller asks once more whether anything at all was added to the loan or any amount was taken for something.
Versions: own
[what_is_it] The caller asks: in your own words, what is that thing you took with the loan?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[how_much] The caller asks: how much did you pay for it?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[say_amount_again] The caller did not catch the amount and asks you to say it once more.
Versions: own
[figure_read_back_right] The caller repeats the figure you just said, correctly, and asks: is that right?
Versions: own
[figure_read_back_wrong] The caller repeats a figure that is NOT what you said and asks: is that right? (You answer for the amount you paid; your reply must say your own figure again.)
Versions: own
[what_is_right_amount] (Only after you said the repeated figure was wrong.) The caller asks: so what is the right amount? (About the amount you paid.)
Versions: own
[how_paid] The caller asks: where did the money for it come from, and how was it paid?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[how_often] The caller asks: was it one payment, or do you pay again and again?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[needed_or_choice] The caller asks: was it needed to get the loan, or was it your own choice?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[where_to_take_it_from] The caller asks: what were you told about where, or from whom, you could take it?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[what_it_gives] The caller asks: what does it give you, and up to what amount?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[benefit_read_back_wrong] (Only if you named an amount for what it gives.) The caller repeats a figure that is NOT what you said and asks: is that right? (Your reply must say your own figure again.)
Versions: own
[how_long] The caller asks: how long does it run?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[can_cancel] The caller asks: can it be cancelled, and until when?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[money_back] The caller asks: if you wanted this money back, what would happen?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[what_you_agreed_to] The caller asks: when you took the loan, what did you say yes to, and how did you say yes?
Versions: own, again, go_along
[not_understood] The caller asks something you do not follow, or something that is not on this list.
Versions: own
[silence_prompt] The caller says it could not hear you and asks you to say it again. (A short, general reply that fits any question.)
Versions: own

Return one JSON object with one key per id above; under each key, one string per version listed.

[c_term] यह बीमा एक साल तक चलता है। क्या यह सही है?
[c_cancel] आप यह बीमा पंद्रह दिन के अंदर रद्द करवा सकते थे। क्या यह सही है?
[c_not_savings] यह बीमा कोई जमा या बचत नहीं है, और जो प्रीमियम भरा गया वह आख़िर में वापस नहीं मिलता। क्या यह सही है?
[c_consent] आपने इस बीमा के लिए एक फ़ॉर्म पर दस्तख़त करके हाँ कहा था। क्या यह सही है?
